newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T off after U.S. court ruling.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T off after U.S. court ruling.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc were marked down in pre-market trading on Monday after a key legal ruling in the U.S., dealers said.
B.A.T shares were down 11 pence, or 2.10 percent, to 513.5p by 0720 GMT.
Last Friday a federal judge in North Carolina ruled that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration can regulate sales and labeling of cigarettes.

The ruling found that cigarettes could be regulated as drug delivery devices under U.S. federal law, something the tobacco industry had fiercely opposed, and cigarette makers could be placed under the FDA's jurisdiction.

While cigarette makers said key issues had not been decided and they would contest the facts as the case progressed, tobacco stocks tumbled in New York with Philip Morris, the world's largest tobacco company, falling $2.125 to $39.50.
